data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘कनक’ (Kanaka), meaning ‘golden’, ‘yellow’, or ‘radiant’. In Hindu mythology, Kanak refers to Lord Indra, the god of rain and thunder, who is also symbolized by gold. This name embodies the spirit of beauty, prosperity, and divinity. The name Kanak carries the meaning “Golden, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kanak usually hope their child will grow to embody golden, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
